vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: brainstorming
Version: 0.1.0

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its instructions for the AI agent to access the file system and execute git commands. Specifically, `SKILL.md` instructs the agent to "Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)" and "Commit the design document to git". While these actions are plausibly needed for the stated purpose of a design and documentation skill, they represent high-risk capabilities (file system read/write and shell command execution) that, according to the provided threshold, warrant a 'suspicious' classification even without clear malicious intent.

llm.summary: This brainstorming skill is mostly coherent, but it can trigger very broadly and instructs the agent to create and commit design documents without a clearly separate approval step.

dimensions.detail: Reading files, docs, and recent commits is proportionate for design planning, but writing under docs/plans and committing to git expands the workflow beyond advisory brainstorming.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is a single Markdown skill file with no bundled executable code, dependencies, remote payload retrieval, or install-time script behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The description says the skill MUST be used before any creative work, which is broader than planning-only use and could intercept many normal implementation tasks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill directs the agent to write a persistent design file and commit it to git after validation, without an explicit separate confirmation for repository mutation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is collaborative design planning, and most instructions support that by gathering project context, asking clarifying questions, comparing approaches, and drafting a design.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you do not want planning conversations to create files or commits automatically. It appears suitable as a design-planning helper only if you are comfortable requiring explicit user confirmation before any docs/plans write or git commit.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad mandatory trigger is supported by the artifact description and is not necessary for a brainstorming aid; this supports Review rather than maliciousness.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The file-write and git-commit instructions are present in the After the Design section; saving a design can fit the purpose, but automatic repository mutation is under-scoped for a planning skill.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The git commit instruction is artifact-backed and creates persistent version-control side effects without a clear separate approval gate.
